verifications.claim: Gary Woodland underwent brain surgery to remove a tumor in September 2023.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'underwent surgery to remove part of a lesion from his brain in September 2023'; R3: 'In September 2023, he had surgery... to remove much of the lesion'; R4: 'operation to remove a brain tumour in September 2023'; R5: 'surgery to remove a brain lesion in 2023'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm surgery in September 2023 to remove a brain lesion/tumor.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland has battled severe PTSD, anxiety, and fear following September 2023 brain surgery.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder as a result of the brain surgery... fear and anxiety'; R2: 'struggles with post-traumatic stress disorder... diagnosed... after undergoing surgery'; R3: 'PTSD... lesion... caused unfounded fears'; R5: 'diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder... following surgery... anxiety and hyper-awareness'
verifications.reasoning: All sources link PTSD, fear, and anxiety directly to post-surgery struggles.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland openly shared in March 2026 that despite returning to the PGA Tour, he struggled with mental fatigue, panic, and felt like he was "dying inside" while competing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'just weeks after Woodland revealed... "Inside, I feel like I’m dying"'; R5: 'March 2026 interview... "inside, I feel like I’m dying"... hypervigilant... symptoms suddenly overwhelmed him on the course'
verifications.reasoning: March 2026 interview (R5 dated 2026/03/09, weeks before March 29 win) directly quotes 'dying' and describes panic-like symptoms while competing post-return.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland's tumor was on the part of his brain controlling fear and anxiety.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'fear and anxiety that he just couldn’t escape'; R3: 'lesion on the part of his brain that caused unfounded fears that he was dying'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly attribute the lesion/tumor location to causing fear and anxiety symptoms.

verifications.claim: Post-surgery, Gary Woodland suffered from fear of dying and intense, recurring anxiety.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'fear and anxiety... jolted awake... nightmare that he was falling and going to die'; R3: 'unfounded fears that he was dying'
verifications.reasoning: Direct descriptions of post-surgery fear of dying and anxiety nightmares/seizures.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland returned to play in early 2024.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'returned to the Tour months later' (after Sept 2023); R3: 'returned in January 2024'; R5: 'returned to TOUR competition in January 2024'

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland often cried in the scoring trailer or his car.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland experienced intense, overwhelming symptoms at the 2024 Procore Championship.
verifications.label: INCORRECT

verifications.reasoning: Symptoms at Procore supported, but timeline ('last fall' from 2026 = 2025, not 2024) contradicts specific 2024 date.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland experienced memory issues at the 2024 Procore Championship.
